findings.problem: shutdown() now closes the writer before writing and flushing the pending items, so the pending output is written to a closed writer.
findings.reason: The diff hunk moves `writer.close()` from the last line of the function (base line 5) to the first statement (head line 2). This inverts the conventional writer lifecycle write -> flush -> close into close -> write -> flush. On the ordinary shutdown path with non-empty pending, every `writer.write(item)` and the final `writer.flush()` now target a closed writer; for standard file-like writers (e.g. Python file/socket-like objects) writes after close either raise (e.g. ValueError: I/O operation on closed file) or silently discard the bytes, and flush after close is a no-op or error. The base revision delivered all pending output before closing; the head revision can therefore lose pending work or abort the shutdown path with an exception. Uncertainty note: the concrete writer implementations live in uncaptured related files (client.py, formatting.py, policy.py, schema.py, test_formatting.py are recorded as missing in repository-context.json), so the exact failure mode (exception versus silent data loss) depends on the writer's post-close contract, but under the standard contract that close terminates output, no ordering other than write-then-flush-then-close delivers the pending items.
